summary: Zesho Machida worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as bettō at Kuon-ji (attested 1990) and professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

Zev Handel works in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and the University of California, Berkeley (1992, 1998). He became a professor at the University of Washington around 1999 and taught Zhihua Li.
Zhao Luo specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied under Sen Wang and was attested in 2014 as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He held an affiliation at Stanford University (attested 2007), taught Kevin Buckelew, and was a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 2018).
Zhen Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned an MA at the University of Munich by 2005 and an MA at Lanzhou University by 2009.
Zhengyan Fan works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, he was a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Buddhist Institute (1947) and under Yinshun (1952). He managed the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992) and taught Chien Y. Hsu.

Zhihua Yao works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002), taught at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005), and joined The Chinese University of Hong Kong around 2005.

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. She held an associate professorship at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and adjunct faculty status at Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

Zhiyi Yang specializes in Sinology. She studied at Peking University and earned her PhD at Princeton University under Martin Kern. She has held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where she was an instructional consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Bai Su (~1952–1956). He served as director at The Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University (~1960–1965). A specialist in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held positions at Peking University, Soka University (1999), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poh Tho Si in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li specializes in Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as studying at Komazawa University and holding a DC research fellowship from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a linguist and Central Asian studies scholar. He attended the Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium until 1895, studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1895–1900), and taught Lajos Ligeti.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyuto Monastery under Dechen Nyingpo and Trijang Rinpoche. He served as abbot of Ganden Shartse and head of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Zsóka Gelle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna, and has held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College, the University of Vienna, and Eötvös Loránd University.
Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1903–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1908–1910).
